AI agents now move funds onchain. But when one acts, nobody can check what it was allowed to do, or what really happened.
So start with a refusal. On Monad mainnet, the Treasury Agent tried to withdraw. The firewall reverted with Function Not Allowed, and nothing was sent.

Every allowed action follows one path. Identity in Agent Registry. Policy in Agent Firewall. Execution only through the firewall. Agent Proof re-checks the receipt, fourteen of fourteen, and anchors the hash. A separate check judges the outcome, and the verdict goes to the official E R C 8004 registries.
It's live on mainnet. The WMON Agent wraps real Wrapped MON, behind a firewall that allows only deposit and transfer.
Don't trust us. Paste an execution id, and the server rebuilds the proof hash from public RPC, and compares it with the onchain anchor. Pass.
For builders, it's one install. Trace Call routes the transaction through the firewall and returns the proof. It also ships as an MCP server.
Why Monad? Anchoring a proof costs about a hundred seventy-nine thousand gas, and finality lands in roughly six hundred milliseconds. Verification keeps pace with the agent.
AgentTrace. Live now on Monad mainnet.
